summary: We built a base building game where the objective is to expand and survive as long as possible on the lunar surface. It addresses the challenge by teaching young kids the importance of managing your resources, planning ahead, taking precautionary actions during unprecedented weather events, and the sacrifices demanded of the human body.
details: Our project runs an internal timer to simulate the passage of days on the lunar surface. It increments supplies such as food, water, oxygen, and power gathered automatically through various buildings. At the same time, it decrements astronauts' health due to radiation exposure and fractures/accidents, bone density, and increases stress. All of these can be accelerated or restored up to a maximum through careful planning and remaining proactive. The intended impact is for aspiring astronauts to understand the precautionary aptitude needed to colonize the moon. The benefit is that through simulating actual complications that occur to the physical body and man-made structures on the moon, players can learn each real-world scenario cause and effect. The tools/languages we used include: JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Python to pull NASA data, Canvas 2D, IndexedDB, Git, GitHub, Node.js, Vercel, Claude Code, and NASA provided resources (data). Our project is creative because it takes the environmental hazards brought about by the lunar surface and places them in a base-building simulator, where the primary goal is to expand, survive, and thrive against odds that are overwhelmingly stacked against humanity. The team considered many factors in the game design process, including but not limited to: deciding which buildings and/or vehicles protect you fully from radiation, to the speed of a simulated day on the moon, to how players could gain additional astronauts to scale their colony, what astronaut roles could perform what functions, and balancing of starter resources, resource generation, and rate of complications faced by the player in-game.
